title: The ordinary inverse-image comparisons commute around a restriction cube
statement: Let r be a coherent ringed Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-strict-tower-operations], let j:U→Y be any scheme map, and let C:OpenCube r j be the eight-vertex shared coefficient presentation [def-sf-ringed-restriction-open-cube]. The six ordinary module inverse-image square comparisons satisfy the cube equation: local target pullback of the base-face comparison, followed by the target-face comparison and upper restriction of the global comparison, equals the local comparison followed by local upper pullback of the source-face comparison and the upper-face comparison. The equation holds on every module over r.RY. It involves no complexes, derived categories, direct images or exchange mates and needs no openness, nonemptiness or finiteness assumption.

source.place: Tag 03CB, composition of morphisms of sites; proetale.tex Tag 09A5, morphisms of pro-etale sites. Ordinary inverse-image coherence in step 7 of lem-sf-ringed-restriction-exchange-open-descent.

proof.text: Expand each exchangeModuleSquare as the inverse ordinary compositor for the first path, transport along the equality of coefficient-decorated composite scheme maps, and the ordinary compositor for the second path. The Cartesian-square commutativity equations identify the underlying composite maps; the coefficient coherence equations of the four side faces and the global and local squares identify the composite ring isomorphisms.

Conjugate the compositors under the composite module adjunctions. Their normalized conjugates act on sections by the fibre-product pasting isomorphisms. The two threefold pastings preserve all three projections, so fibre-product uniqueness identifies them. Injectivity of conjugation transfers this associativity to the module inverse-image compositors. This is the composition coherence for morphisms of sites applied to the transported module actions.

Substitute compositor associativity into the two six-face paths and cancel the inverse compositor pairs. Coefficient equality transports compose by equality elimination. This gives precisely the displayed ordinary cube equation, including for the zero module and empty schemes.

lean.statement:
theorem restriction_pullback_cube
    {X' X Y' Y U : Scheme.{u}} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ Y'}
    {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y' ⟶ Y} {sq : ChosenCartesianSquare g' f' f g}
    (r : StrictTowerRingedSquare sq) {j : U ⟶ Y} (C : OpenCube r j)
    (M : proEtaleRingModules Y r.RY) :
    (targetPull C.localRings).map (C.baseFace.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app M) ≫
        C.targetFace.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app ((basePull r).obj M) ≫
        (upperPull C.targetFace).map (r.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app M) =
      C.localRings.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app ((basePull C.sourceFace).obj M) ≫
        (upperPull C.localRings).map (C.sourceFace.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app M) ≫
        C.upperFace.exchangeModuleSquare.hom.app ((verticalPull r).obj M)
